text:
elena: Quick heads-up — tenant `acme-corp` spiked into our failover region yesterday and blew past their Regional QPS quota. We only noticed in billing alerts. Any ideas why failover traffic isn't counted against primary-region quotas?

sam: Hmm. Are we applying quotas before or after routing? I thought quota check was at the ingress based on intended region header.

elena: We check quotas at the origin service but routing happens earlier in the gateway. When gateway fails over, the request lands in another region and the origin enforces a different quota bucket. So from billing POV it's fine, but product-level quotas look wrong and tenants see inconsistent limits.

marius: Could be precedence: route matching -> header overrides -> failover. Proposal: add per-tenant region preference that the gateway honors and does quota attribution to the preferred region unless tenant explicitly allows cross-region. API sketch: `route.region_preference = ["us-west-2", "us-east-1"]` and `X-Tenant-Region-Override: deny|allow` header.

priya: UX question: if we expose region preference in Console, should we show a simple fallback order UI (drag to reorder) or a weight slider? We want both latency-based and legal residency support.

lucas: Weighting + SLOs is tricky. If we do weights, we need to surface expected latency/cost tradeoffs and ensure quotas are enforced on the effective target region. Otherwise a weighted split could exceed tenant capacity in one region.

anne: For telemetry, tag routed requests with `target_region`, `fallback_step` (e.g., primary_unavailable, probe_timeout), and `tenant_region_preference` so dashboards can attribute correctly. Also add `fallback_reason` to traces. That'll make debugging and billing reconciliation easier.

ops-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026-459 — high cross-region quota usage for tenant acme-corp (auto-created from billing alert).

sam: Quick mitigation: we can add a gateway-side feature flag to prefer primary-region routing for all authenticated tenants for 24h while we design the API. Curl to set header at proxy level: `curl -H "X-Region-Preference: us-west-2" -H "X-Tenant-Lock: true" https://gateway.redwood.example/v1/generate`

marius: Long term: API + console + telemetry + quota-binding. RFC idea: binding a tenant to a primary region for quota attribution, with explicit opt-in for cross-region failover. Also automatic rollback to cost-optimized fallback depending on SLAs.

priya: I can take Console UX work — will mock drag-order + toggle for "Strict quota attribution" and a weight slider for experimental canary.

elena: Awesome. I'll draft the RFC and a small gateway shim for the flag. @marius can you own the quota-binding design? @lucas please validate cost/slo implications. I'll schedule a canary rollout after initial tests.

deploy-bot: Scheduled canary: gateway-region-preference-flag -> canary in us-west-2 starting in 30m (will post status).

elena: Thanks — will follow up with RFC link and a quick sync.
